stem.text: In an investigation, the same concentration of the enzyme phosphorylase was added to different concentrations of glucose phosphate and incubated at $30\,{}^{\circ}\text{C}$. At 1 minute intervals, one drop of the reaction mixture was removed and added to a drop of iodine solution on a white tile.
The diagram shows the results of this investigation.

stem.alt: Grid of dots: columns for concentration of glucose phosphate in mg dm−3 from 0 to 35 in steps of 5, rows for time in minutes from 0 to 9; each dot is brown or black. Key: colour of iodine solution, brown and black.

stem.text: What explains the trend in the results of this investigation?

A.text: Phosphorylase catalyses a reaction converting glucose phosphate to starch.

B.text: The maximum rate of reaction is reached at $20\,\text{mg dm}^{-3}$ of glucose phosphate.

C.text: Substrate concentration is limiting at concentrations of glucose phosphate $25\,\text{mg dm}^{-3}$ or less.

D.text: Enzyme concentration is limiting at concentrations of glucose phosphate $25\,\text{mg dm}^{-3}$ or less.
